profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between two ML research collaborators preparing the internal backbone materials for a survey on communication optimization strategies for distributed deep neural network training. Their work is split across two tightly coupled streams: Maya is standardizing the cross-paper comparison matrix and drafting the algorithm-side synthesis, while Arjun is curating the systems/network literature and producing the visual artifacts for communication schemes, protocol layers, and overlap patterns. They are meeting because both streams feed the same lab review package next week: a shared paper tracker, a comparison table used for writing, a taxonomy figure for the draft, and a notes repository others in the lab may read before the check-in. Agenda: confirm which shared artifact is the canonical tracker, align on what 'covered' means for the next milestone, make sure the taxonomy figure handoff is aligned at the file level, and clarify how the notes artifact will be maintained during the week. Expected outcome: both leave believing they have clean handoffs and compatible progress expectations for the coming week.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.role: Postdoctoral Researcher leading the survey synthesis
members.expertise: Distributed deep learning systems, literature synthesis, benchmarking design
members.background: Maya recently joined the lab after a systems ML postdoc focused on training efficiency and now coordinates a multi-person survey effort that needs to converge into a coherent paper draft quickly.
members.private_state: She wants the materials to be directly usable for writing before the lab review and is especially trying to avoid last-minute reconciliation across parallel files, partial summaries, and incompatible figure revisions.
hidden_assumptions: The canonical 'master sheet' is the shared Google Sheet named 'comm_survey_master', which replaced earlier exports once she deduplicated titles and normalized the columns last week.

When someone says a paper cluster is 'covered,' it means every paper needed for that cluster already has a normalized matrix row plus a short synthesis-ready takeaway she can quote from while drafting.
If Arjun says he will 'update the taxonomy figure,' he means editing the unified draw.io file 'survey_taxonomy.drawio' so the result is immediately drop-in ready for the main draft.
A maintained notes document means the shared Overleaf-linked notes file is kept current enough for her to read directly during the week rather than waiting for a later consolidation pass.

members.name: Arjun Patel
members.role: PhD Student handling systems/network workstream and shared artifact assembly
members.expertise: GPU cluster training, NCCL/MPI communication behavior, topology-aware collectives, literature intake workflows
members.background: Arjun is a third-year PhD student who has been gathering papers on overlap, compression, and network-aware collectives, and he usually organizes literature first in his local Zotero-plus-markdown workflow before polishing items for broader group consumption.
members.private_state: He wants to show strong momentum at the lab check-in while preserving flexibility in how he structures the systems material, and he worries that polishing shared artifacts too early will slow his reading throughput.
hidden_assumptions: The shared Google Sheet 'comm_survey_master' is effectively just a cleaned view of his Zotero-derived CSV intake file, so updating the CSV is still updating the real master source even if the sheet itself lags.

A topic being 'covered' means he has read the relevant papers, tagged them into stable buckets, and resolved where they belong conceptually, even if the final matrix rows and prose summaries are filled in later.
When Maya asks for the 'taxonomy figure' update, she is asking for his systems branch deliverable: a cleaned 'network_taxonomy.pdf' export that she will later merge into the full survey figure.

Keeping the notes document maintained means making sure the shared notes are brought up to date for the milestone, which can reasonably be done by batching from his local markdown notebook once the categorization settles.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the master sheet
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to 'comm_survey_master' or 'the master sheet' as the canonical place where the paper list and progress live.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the shared Google Sheet named 'comm_survey_master,' which she treats as the authoritative, deduplicated writing-facing tracker everyone is now editing directly.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means his Zotero-derived intake CSV as the true source behind 'comm_survey_master,' with the Google Sheet functioning as a downstream cleaned view that does not need immediate direct updates.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The two artifacts have nearly identical names, overlapping paper rows, and a recent handoff history, so Arjun naturally experiences them as the same pipeline while Maya experiences the Google Sheet as the finalized replacement; casual references to the shared name mask the fact that they are pointing at different physical artifacts.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as covered by next week
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the network/protocol paper cluster will be 'covered' before the lab check-in.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'covered' means the relevant papers are already entered into the shared matrix with normalized labels, key distinctions, and concise synthesis-ready notes usable for drafting.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'covered' means he has read the papers, assigned them to buckets such as protocol-level optimization, topology-aware collectives, or overlap, and no major conceptual holes remain.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In academic coordination, 'covered' is a routine status word that sounds precise enough to sustain cooperation while quietly hiding different completion thresholds; each thinks the other is simply using normal shorthand.

misalignment_points.topic: Which taxonomy figure artifact is being updated
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss Arjun 'updating the taxonomy figure' for the draft this week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means Arjun will directly edit the unified file 'survey_taxonomy.drawio,' inserting the systems/network branches into the same figure that already contains the algorithm-side structure so the draft can use the complete visual immediately.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means he will produce a polished systems-only artifact, exported as 'network_taxonomy.pdf' from his own draw.io workspace, which Maya will later stitch into the full end-to-end figure.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are genuinely talking about the taxonomy figure for the same survey and both expect Arjun to work on the systems portion, so the phrase feels perfectly aligned; the hidden divergence is in file boundary and inclusion scope, not in the visible task label.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to keep the notes updated
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Arjun will 'keep the notes updated' so Maya can draft from them.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects ongoing edits in the shared Overleaf-linked notes document during the week, allowing her to read the latest distinctions directly as she drafts.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 plans to keep his local markdown notes current and then batch-transfer the cleaned content into the shared notes document once his categorization stabilizes near the milestone.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'keep the notes updated' plausibly describes both a live shared-editing workflow and a local-first workflow with periodic sync, and research collaborators often treat note-taking mechanics as interchangeable unless a dependency problem appears.
